text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele made a TV speech to report about the country's present situation. He said GDP was growing more than before but talked also about crime, politics and the demographic situation.
- The president of Hungary, Arpad Goncz, arrived on a two-day official visit to Latvia.
- The new Norwegian-owned Rimi supermarket received an anonymous threat on e-mail.
- Parliament passed a law on the free economic zone in the eastern town, expected to boost economic development in the poverty-struck region.
- Following a TV adress by Shkele where he attacked the Social Democrats, the leader of Latvia's Social Democrats, Juris Bojars, said he will bring a suit against Shkele.
- Former Prime Minister Maris Gailis launched his book of memoirs, "The technlogy of power".
- The ministry of finance lodged a suit against pharmaceutical firm Grindex to cancel an agreement under which the company was given a credit of $6.8 million for failing to pay interests in due time.
- Talks between Latvia and Estonia on the territorial waters of both countries ended with no result. Estonia fears Latvia will fish too much in the Estonian part of the Gulf of Riga.
- The chief manager of Riga commercial port, Gunars Ross, was sacked on Thursday, according to unofficial information by Dienas Bizness.
